info: Tracer through rock · peclet = 100.0, injection = Pulse · 684×648
label: peclet = 100.0, injection = Pulse

derived.label: Péclet number
derived.note: Pe = u·d/D_m; the molecular diffusivity is set from the pore speed measured once the flow has settled

derived.label: flow time steps
derived.note: the flow is settled first, then held fixed

plots.title: Breakthrough at the outlet
plots.explain: Flux-averaged concentration of the water leaving the sample, Σuc/Σu over the outlet face: what a sampler at the end of a column measures, not a plain average over the last cells. The outlet is open, so tracer leaves and never returns. A slug was released at the inlet, so the curve rises, peaks and decays; its tail is the tracer held back in slow channels and dead ends. One pore-volume crossing at the mean advective speed takes about 1.07e+05 lattice steps, and half of the peak arrives at 3.97e+04. Arrival earlier than the crossing time means the tracer found fast channels. Treat this as qualitative: the pore Reynolds number is 1.84, so this is not the creeping flow that holding the field fixed assumes.

plots.title: How fast the plume spreads
plots.explain: Variance of the pore-averaged concentration profile along the flow. For pure diffusion it grows as 2·D_m·t; the slope of the measured curve, fitted while the plume is still inside the sample (the fit stops once a fifth has left through the open outlet), gives an effective spreading coefficient D_eff = 2.98e-01 cells²/step, which is 162 times the molecular value at Pe = 100. Spreading beyond the molecular value is mechanical dispersion, neighbouring channels carrying the tracer at different speeds, so long as it also stands clear of the scheme's own numerical diffusion, which here is about 2.05e-02. The measured spreading is above the numerical diffusion of the advection scheme, so it reflects the pore-scale velocity field.

plots.title: The plume as it crosses the sample
plots.explain: Concentration averaged across the sample at each position along the flow, pore cells only, at the start, the middle and the end of the run. A symmetric hump means diffusion dominates; a steep front with a long tail behind it means the velocity field is doing the spreading.

notes: the pore Reynolds number is 1.84, not the creeping flow that Darcy's law and a frozen velocity field assume
